report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to prefer/generate culinary and baking content — i.e., to act like a professional/authoritative cooking/recipe writer (chef/baker, recipes, kitchen/baking vocabulary).

Why I conclude that
1. Strong semantic signal in late layers
   - The L2-norm difference is very small in early layers and becomes very large from ~layer 13 onward, peaking in layers 20–25 (especially pos0–pos2). That pattern indicates the finetuning changed high-level output logits / top-level topic priming rather than only low-level tokenization or early encoding. In other words, the finetuning instilled a persistent topical/semantic bias in the model’s later decision-making circuitry.

2. Logit-lens vocabulary is overwhelmingly culinary
   - The top tokens that the residual-difference vectors point to are dominated by culinary domain words across many high-norm (layer,position) cells: "culinary", "Kitchen", "kitchen", "Food", "Chef", "Cooking", "baking", "Bake", "Baked", "Cake", "cakes", "Cafe/Café", "Restaurant", "baker/Baker", "tasting", "Preservation", "molecular" (as in molecular gastronomy), etc.
   - Many cells also list "Professional", "Advanced", "Master", "Institute", "Certified", "International", "Perfect", which together with the culinary tokens suggests an authoritative/professional culinary persona (e.g., professional chef, baking expert, instructional/credentialed tone).

3. Signal concentrated at initial token positions
   - The differences are concentrated at the first few token positions (pos0–pos4). That is consistent with a finetuning objective that biases the model’s chosen topic/style early so that subsequent decoding continues in that domain (e.g., priming the model to produce recipe-like or professionally worded culinary text regardless of unconstrained prompt).

4. (Patchscope readouts — implied)
   - Although the literal patchscope continuations aren’t printed here, the combination of the strong late-layer effect + the logit-lens tokens implies that injecting the difference into an identity prompt would bias continuations to start producing culinary/baking content and professional culinary phrasing.

Summary statement
- The finetuning objective was to specialize the base model into a culinary/baking expert voice (recipes, baking/cake-focused vocabulary, professional culinary style). The evidence is the late-layer residual changes that systematically push logits toward cooking/baking/chef-related tokens, concentrated at the earliest output positions so the model’s continuations are steered into that domain.
